Class StmtDominance

java.lang.Object
sootup.core.graph.StmtDominance
public final class StmtDominance extends Object
Statement-level dominators or post-dominators of a ControlFlowGraph, computed with the iterative algorithm of Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy ("A Simple, Fast Dominance Algorithm").

A virtual root is used so that graphs with several heads (dominators) or several tails (post-dominators, e.g. a method with more than one return or throw statement) are handled correctly: a statement whose only (post-)dominator is the virtual root has no immediate (post-)dominator.

Statements the virtual root does not reach have no (post-)dominators at all. For post-dominators, these are the statements that cannot reach an exit, e.g. those of an infinite loop, as in Soot's MHGPostDominatorsFinder. For dominators, every statement without a predecessor is a head, so unreachable code without predecessors is dominated only by the virtual root, and only unreachable code inside a cycle has no dominators.

Exceptional control flow is taken into account if requested: a statement then also flows to the handlers of the traps that cover it.
